feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital communications/platform roles: the experience is relevant, progressive, and supported by concrete scope indicators (10,000+ pages, 3.5M page views, 50+ publishers). It reads clearly and professionally, but impact would improve with more outcome-focused results, less repetition across skills sections, and a few style/grammar fixes.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear leadership narrative with steady progression at NACo into director/consulting scope; positioning is well aligned to public-sector digital leadership.  
- Good use of scale metrics and specific platforms/tools (Drupal, GA4, BigQuery, Power BI), which strengthens credibility.  
- Writing is generally polished, concise, and strategically framed around modernization, governance, analytics, and multimedia.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more measurable outcomes beyond scope: e.g., traffic growth, engagement uplift, production savings, campaign performance, search improvements, or workflow efficiency gains.  
- Reduce duplication between Core Competencies, Topline Skills, and Technical + IT; consolidate to create a tighter structure and more space for achievements.  
- Fix stylistic/grammar inconsistencies: “social, and multimedia” should be “social and multimedia”; maintain consistent serial-comma usage; “A2/Learning” is awkward—use “A2 (learning)”; “Coleman DAVIS” capitalization may look inconsistent unless intentional branding. No major misspellings found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and sector focus, but it reads broad and repeats themes already covered in the subtitle, competencies, and experience. It would be stronger with one or two concrete scale signals and tighter phrasing.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace generic “building the platforms” language with sharper action verbs and outcomes; e.g., “Leads enterprise web modernization, governance, analytics, and editorial operations for high-volume public-sector communications.”
- Add a concrete scale marker from recent experience to increase impact, such as “10,000+ page website,” “3.5M annual page views,” or “50+ internal publishers.”
- Trim the list slightly to avoid sounding exhaustive; “multimedia production” and “AI-enabled user experiences” can stay, but the sentence should prioritize most relevant leadership areas.
- Consider this rewrite: “Digital platform and communications leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing public-sector web ecosystems, governance, analytics, and editorial operations. Led transformation of a 10,000+ page Drupal platform serving 3.5M annual page views, while building scalable content, multimedia, and AI-enabled discovery systems.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital leader” overlaps with the subtitle; vary the phrasing.
- The capability list closely mirrors Core Competencies, so avoid repeating every domain here.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and work experience. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing higher-level leadership capabilities will make it feel less repetitive and more executive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel, concise noun phrases and reduce “operations” repetition.
- Prioritize strategic, recent strengths over broad communications wording.
- Consider this version: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial systems • Analytics, reporting, and insight infrastructure • Workflow automation and platform integration • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Multi-channel communications leadership • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia production and livestream delivery
- If targeting more technical roles, swap “Public-sector advocacy communications” for “CMS and digital platform delivery.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise website modernization,” “AI-enabled search,” “analytics infrastructure,” and “multimedia production” are already reinforced in the header and Topline Skills.
- “Multi-channel communications operations” overlaps with several NACo roles; “leadership” is stronger and less repetitive.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it largely repeats achievements already covered in recent NACo roles. Tightening phrasing and adding clearer outcomes or scope would make it feel more distinct and higher impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a one-line intro such as “Selected recent projects” and keep each item to one crisp, parallel sentence.
- Emphasize what was delivered and why it mattered: e.g., “AI legislative search experience,” “Drupal 10 campaign microsite,” “interactive conference installation.”
- Use consistent action/result structure: “Built/Developed [project] to [business/user outcome].”
- Standardize style and punctuation; spell out “10-by-20-foot” for cleaner CV formatting.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and advocacy video series closely overlap with the 2024–Present and 2018–2024 NACo bullets.
- “Organization Anniversary Campaign” is the most distinct item; consider prioritizing similarly unique projects here to avoid repetition.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: coleman@colemanpdavis.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the NACo roles below and the Recent Projects section. Tighten it around consultant-level scope, strategic value, and 2–3 concrete outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope and seniority: “Advise NACo on enterprise digital strategy, web modernization, and cross-channel communications operations as an external consultant.”
- Consolidate execution bullets into 3 impact-focused bullets, e.g. strategy/operations, Drupal campaign builds, AI search initiative.
- Replace generic phrasing (“build and refine,” “advise on best practices”) with outcome language: “streamlined workflows,” “improved content governance,” “launched modular Drupal campaign experiences.”
- Add measurable signals where possible: number of sites/campaigns launched, publishers supported, workflow time reduced, search/discovery improvements, toolkit downloads, engagement lift.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search initiative” and Drupal microsite work duplicate the Recent Projects section; keep this entry higher-level and let projects hold the detail.
- “Governance, usability, workflows, analytics” repeats the 2022–2024 Director role; emphasize external advisory/consulting scope instead.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management details already covered in adjacent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper scope/result line: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance and budget, leading platform modernization and organization-wide communications operations.”
- Combine and streamline bullets around the website and analytics work: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users and 50+ internal publishers; expanded analytics stack across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery to improve reporting and decision-making.”
- Make channel leadership more outcome-focused: add email open/click growth, audience growth, engagement, production volume, or campaign impact if available.
- Rephrase studio/governance bullets to show business value: “Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house studio, increasing internal production capacity for advocacy and events” and “standardized governance, publishing and planning workflows across departments.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry.
- Video-program expansion also appears in earlier NACo roles; keep this version at the infrastructure/leadership level.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this item overlaps heavily with the adjacent NACo roles and reads more as general responsibility than distinct achievement. Make it more specific to what changed under your leadership at this stage.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + function: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, improving editorial coordination for advocacy and member communications.”
- Tighten bullets to 3–4 impact-focused points; e.g., “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Rephrase video bullet to show outcome: “Launched and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine the last two bullets into one stronger systems statement: “Improved editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, increasing consistency and cross-team coordination.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video” is very close to the Director of Digital Media entry.
- “Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update” overlaps with the earlier Digital Media Manager/Producer role and the footer project; keep only if framed as scaling/formalizing the program at this level.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo roles. Tighten it to emphasize senior-level scope and the most current, differentiated strengths.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad phrases with sharper, outcome-oriented wording tied to recent work:
- Enterprise digital strategy for high-volume public-sector platforms
- Editorial governance and cross-team content operations
- Multi-channel communications leadership across web, email, social and video
- Audience-centered advocacy and member communications
- Consider swapping “Audience-focused content planning” for “Campaign and storytelling strategy” to better reflect recent consulting/project work.
- Keep wording parallel and concise; avoid repeating “public-sector” and “digital strategy” elsewhere on the page.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Editorial systems and governance” duplicates Core Competencies (“Digital governance & editorial systems”).
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” is close to Core Competencies (“Advocacy and public-sector communications”).

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill coverage, but this item is too tool-heavy and overlaps heavily with the separate “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, it should emphasize higher-value platform leadership and modernization themes, with only the most relevant tools.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a software list to a capability-led line, e.g.: “Drupal and enterprise CMS platforms • Web modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API and workflow integrations • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search and discovery”
- Drop lower-priority or older-feeling items here if not central to recent work: WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, jQuery.
- Replace “technical execution” phrasing with more senior language if possible: “Web Platforms & CMS Modernization” or “Platform Architecture & Technical Delivery.”
- If space allows, align to recent impact by hinting at scale: “enterprise CMS modernization” or “large public-facing web platforms.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Current list duplicates the “Technical + IT” section almost verbatim.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also repeats Core Competencies; keep it here only if shortened to “AI-enabled search and discovery.”

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for recent leadership roles, but it reads as a tool list rather than a value statement. It also overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section, so this version should emphasize strategic application over platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability-led phrasing, e.g. “Analytics strategy, dashboarding & optimization” rather than a pure software list.
- Tighten and group items: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity” + “KPI framework design, executive reporting, SEO/performance analysis.”
- Consider a sharper rewrite: “Analytics strategy • KPI design • Executive dashboarding/reporting • GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity • SEO and performance optimization”
- If space allows elsewhere, connect to impact in experience bullets instead of here: reporting that improved decision-making, visibility, or channel performance.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT; keep Topline Skills more strategic and leave full tool inventory to Technical + IT.
- “Leadership reporting” may be better phrased as “executive reporting” for clarity and seniority.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it reads generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and older NACo multimedia bullets. Make it sharper, more senior, and tied to delivery environments rather than basic tasks.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with a tighter, more differentiated list such as:
- Broadcast-quality video production and post-production
- Livestream and hybrid event delivery
- In-house studio buildout and operations
- PTZ camera and multi-camera production workflows
- Virtual event and advocacy content production
- Consider dropping “video production and editing” for “broadcast-quality video production and post-production” to sound more leadership-level.
- Use “livestream and hybrid event delivery” instead of separate generic terms for concision.
- If space allows elsewhere, add a measurable proof point tied to the NACo studio buildout or recurring video programming.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” already appears in Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same phrasing.
- “Studio operations” and “PTZ camera systems” risk sounding too tactical unless balanced with higher-level delivery language.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This item should either add specificity or be tightened to avoid repetition.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to emphasize strongest/recent platforms first: **Drupal (enterprise migration, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, add light proficiency/context instead of a bare list, e.g. **Drupal (primary) • WordPress • SharePoint intranets • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Consider dropping the title “Web Platforms & CMS” for **CMS & Web Platforms** for cleaner phrasing.
- If you want more impact, replace weakest/least-used item with a more current platform only if supported elsewhere in the CV.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates Topline Skills [2], which already lists Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, and Power Pages.
- GitHub Pages is not reinforced elsewhere; keep it only if you can point to real project use or remove it.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” For a senior digital leader, this item should emphasize implementation depth and modern tools rather than basic languages alone.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from raw languages to capability-based phrasing: “Front-end implementation (HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery) • API and tag management integrations • Edge/serverless scripting (Cloudflare Workers) • Deployment automation (GitHub Actions)”
- Consider dropping version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless required; “HTML/CSS” is cleaner and more current.
- If accurate, add scope or outcome-oriented qualifiers: “API integrations for CMS, analytics and campaign workflows” or “GitHub Actions for deployment and publishing automation.”
- Put the strongest, more distinctive tools later in the list but keep them visible: Cloudflare Workers and GitHub Actions signal more advanced implementation than HTML/CSS.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- Google Tag Manager may fit better under “Data, Analytics & Optimization” to reduce overlap.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item is too broad and reads like a generic software list. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills, so it should be tighter and more role-relevant.

Suggested edit:
- Split automation tools from collaboration/project tools to improve clarity and signal depth.
- Reorder by strongest, most relevant systems first: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier, then project/ops tools.
- Consider renaming to: “Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Tools.”
- Suggested rewrite: “Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Trello • Slack • Microsoft Teams • Basecamp”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable” and “workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills/Core Competencies; keep this section as tools only, not capabilities.
- If space is tight, drop 1–2 lower-value collaboration tools (e.g., Basecamp, Trello) unless used recently in current/2022–present roles.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Relevant tools, but this line is too bare and undersells a clear strength shown across recent NACo roles: enterprise email operations and member communications. It should signal scale and purpose, not just list platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to emphasize capability, e.g. **Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms** or **Email CRM & Member Engagement**.
- Reorder by likely relevance/recency: **Higher Logic • Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Mailchimp** (if Higher Logic was primary at NACo).
- If accurate, add a light qualifier to connect to impact: **Higher Logic (member newsletters at scale) • Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys (journey automation) • Mailchimp**.
- Keep it concise; avoid slash-heavy phrasing. Consider shortening Microsoft naming to **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights (Journeys)**.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item overlaps with work-experience bullets about newsletters reaching tens of thousands; don’t repeat audience-size metrics here unless you remove them elsewhere.
- “Engagement” also overlaps with “Multi-channel communications operations” in Core Competencies, so keep this item tool-focused.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools for the recent NACo leadership work, but this item is generic and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills.” It should emphasize analysis/optimization capability, not just list platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Analytics, Insights & Optimization**
- Tighten and group by function: **GA4 • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • Microsoft Clarity • SEO analysis • A/B testing • KPI dashboarding**
- If space allows, make the wording more outcome-oriented elsewhere in the CV by tying these tools to recent impact, e.g., reporting for a **10,000+ page site / 3.5M annual page views**.
- Keep only tools/methods here; avoid vague nouns like “Dashboarding” unless specified as **KPI dashboarding** or **executive reporting dashboards**.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This is nearly identical to **Topline Skills [3] Analytics, Insights & Optimization**; consider removing one or making this version tool-only and the Topline version capability-focused.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already named in the 2022–2024 role, so don’t repeat extra descriptors here unless they add specificity.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and reads like a setup role rather than showing concrete contributions. Tighten it around team-building, platform/content delivery, and early leadership, with any available scale metrics.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground advancement and outcomes: “Promoted across two digital roles while helping build NACo’s first in-house digital team and formalize workflows across web, email, social and video.”
- Add measurable scope if possible: website refresh size/traffic, number of livestreams or weekly videos produced, audience reach, or growth in output/engagement.
- Make leadership more specific: replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with “supervised/mentored a digital media associate” if accurate.
- Possible version: “Promoted across two digital roles, helping launch NACo’s first in-house digital team and improve workflows across web, email, social and video. Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and mentored a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; distinguish this as launching or early production of the format.
- “Strengthening workflows” is repeated across later roles; frame this here as foundational team/process buildout.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with a credible “first podcast” achievement, but it reads generic and overlaps with later NACo multimedia/digital roles. Emphasize the podcast launch and any concrete project scope or outputs; keep the rest brief.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground the distinctive achievement: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting county policy and program teams; launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, guest coordination and production.”
- Replace vague phrases like “contributed to digital content production” with a sharper support function, e.g., “produced multimedia and digital content to translate research and policy work for member audiences.”
- If possible, add 1 measurable detail: number of episodes, stakeholder groups served, project count, or audience/reach.
- Keep this entry to 1–2 lines since later roles show broader digital leadership.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later Digital Media Manager / Producer and Associate Communications Director entries.
- Avoid overemphasizing general digital coordination here; later roles already establish that progression.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too generic and overlaps heavily with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” elsewhere. Tighten it to software/tools only, and let work experience carry the production/storytelling impact.
